title: Autobiography of a Yogi
author: Paramahansa Yogananda
edition_analyzed: Original English edition, with reference to later authorized editions by Self-Realization Fellowship
target_audience: Seekers of spiritual wisdom and personal transformation
Readers interested in yoga and Indian spirituality
Followers of comparative religion and eastern philosophy
Individuals seeking inspiration or accounts of spiritual teachers
Anyone curious about the lives of historical yogis and saints
core_themes: The universal nature of spiritual truth
The science and practice of Kriya Yoga
The meeting of East and West spiritual traditions
Respect for all faiths and religious tolerance
The importance of a guru-disciple relationship
primary_purpose: To share the extraordinary life journey of Paramahansa Yogananda and introduce readers to the principles of yoga, meditation, and spiritual realization, while also bridging Eastern and Western spiritual traditions.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person memoir, lyrical and descriptive, reflective with anecdotal storytelling
structure_format.organization: Chronological narrative interwoven with spiritual discourse and philosophical insights
features: Detailed accounts of Yogananda's life from childhood through adulthood
Descriptions of encounters with spiritual teachers and saints
Appendices, glossary, and photographs in some editions

key_concepts_lessons: Self-realization and connection to the divine are attainable through disciplined spiritual practice.
Guru-disciple relationships are vital for authentic spiritual progress.
Spiritual experience transcends religious boundaries; there is a universal truth underlying all faiths.
Kriya Yoga is presented as a powerful scientific meditation technique for accelerating spiritual growth.
Faith, devotion, and perseverance are central to overcoming life's challenges.
Material pursuits are secondary to inner realization and service to humanity.
style_tone: Didactic at times, with philosophical exposition
notable_features: Introduced millions in the West to yoga and meditation
Contains detailed, accessible explanations of spiritual concepts
Candid recollections of miracles, saints, holy men, and spiritual experiences
Blends autobiography with comparative religious commentary
Photographic plates and footnotes in authorized editions
cultural_historical_context: Published in 1946, 'Autobiography of a Yogi' was groundbreaking as one of the first detailed accounts to introduce Indian spirituality, yoga philosophy, and the discipline of meditation to a broad Western audience. It reflects a period of growing interest in Eastern wisdom and interfaith dialogue, just after World War II.
reception_impact: Recognized globally as a spiritual classic and perennial bestseller
Influenced spiritual teachers, seekers, and leaders, including Steve Jobs and George Harrison
Established Yogananda as a major figure in bringing yoga and meditation to the West
Translated into multiple languages and used by many as a guide for spiritual practice
Critics note the miraculous accounts may challenge skeptical readers but acknowledge its profound impact on global spirituality
comparable_titles: The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna by Swami Nikhilananda
The Life Divine by Sri Aurobindo
Be Here Now by Ram Dass
Journey to Self-Realization by Paramahansa Yogananda (posthumous collection)
